title: Twenty minutes with GamePlanIQ
intro: A board meeting demo in five acts: a parent, a player, a coach, the league office and the platform. Each step switches to the right person and opens the right screen. Say what is in bold; click what is listed.

acts.title: Act 1 · A parent who never played

steps.title: Tyler's home page
say: Every parent lands on what matters today: field status, the next game, a coach's assignment and a report card waiting.
The digest at the top is the same thing a daily email would say.

steps.title: Jack's report card
say: Coach Galasso rated ten skills, celebrated three, picked one thing to work on, and the app chose the lessons that teach it for a nine-year-old.
Private to the family, the coach and the league. Never a ranking.

steps.title: A lesson for a scared kid
say: Written for the parent who never played: what to do, what to say, what to avoid, a verified drill video, and a ten-minute practice.
Mark done feeds the player's progress and badges.

steps.title: Game-day duties on the team page
say: Snacks, scorekeeper, dugout parent, per game. Parents claim with one tap; the coach can nudge the whole team.
click: I'll do it on the open snack slot

steps.title: One calendar for the family
say: Games, practices, duties, due dates and deadlines in one file with phone reminders. This is how the league reaches a family that never opens an app.

steps.title: Baseball IQ on the diamond
say: Jack's own account: no messages, no leaderboards. Tap where the ball should go; some answers are acceptable, not just right or wrong.
Fifteen lessons and fifty questions, all written for kids.

steps.title: Coaches' Headquarters
say: Mark is a parent with one season of experience. Everything he needs is on one page: practice planner, team tools, game day, certification, tryouts and All-Star ballots.
click: Look at the certification progress and the tryout card

steps.title: Game day: lineup and scorebook
say: The lineup card checks the league's minimum-play rule, bench innings and pitcher rest before first pitch.
The scorebook is one thumb: run, out, pitch count. Final updates standings and rest days in one tap.
click: Scorebook tab, add a run and an out

steps.title: Run a practice from a phone
say: A generated plan becomes a full-screen timer with cues and the drill video one tap away. Finish logs it and sends the home assignment.

steps.title: Tryout scoring board
say: Six stations, one to five, on any phone. Scores from every evaluator roll into the draft board the commissioner runs.
click: Score a player: Save and next

steps.title: Coach certification
say: Six safety and conduct modules with a check at the end. The league sees who is ready to be around players; nobody chases paper.
click: Open the heat and lightning module

steps.title: What needs a decision today
say: Kenny sees the attention list first: documents to review, conflicts, a live draft, coaches not yet certified, fields needing a call.
click: Field status: set the Tee Ball Diamond to open

steps.title: Scheduling with conflict detection
say: Drag a game to another day. Field, team, shared-coach and umpire conflicts are flagged; a rainout closes a field and tells every family in one step.

steps.title: Draft board and All-Stars
say: Tryout scores become a snake draft with balance warnings that advise, never block. All-Star nominations, ballots and the tally live here; only selected families are told.

steps.title: Bringing a league over
say: Paste last season's spreadsheet. Every row is checked and previewed before anything is written.
click: Import CSV, use the example row

steps.title: Communications and notification rules
say: One announcement reaches the right audience. Every notification follows published rules: topic switches, quiet hours, no duplicates.

steps.title: Public website without code
say: Change the headline, publish, and open the public site. No rosters or player names are ever public.

acts.title: Act 5 · Your league, in fifteen minutes

steps.title: Onboard a league
say: Name, colors, season, divisions, teams and fields. The wizard ends on a working league office ready for the CSV import you just saw.
click: Walk the steps, then Create league

closing: Everything you saw runs on one shared database with role-based permissions enforced on every action, not just hidden in menus.
Payments, email and SMS connect at deployment; the in-app record and the family calendar work today.
